tools.name: coder/coder
tools.what: A self-hosted control plane that provisions workspaces from Terraform templates you write.

tools.name: GitHub Codespaces
tools.what: A workspace defined by a file in the repository and hosted by the vendor.

tools.name: Amazon SageMaker
tools.what: A managed hosting and tooling surface: notebooks, training jobs and inference endpoints.

tools.name: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash
tools.what: DeepSeek’s V4 Flash text model, stored mostly in 8-bit and FP8 formats across 46 safetensors shards (about 291 billion parameters as the hub counts them), MIT-licensed and ungated.

tools.name: google/gemma-3-27b-it
tools.what: Google’s 27-billion-parameter instruction-tuned Gemma 3 model, taking images as well as text, 12 safetensors shards, under Google’s own Gemma terms and behind a manual approval gate; the card body returned 401 without a login on 2026-09-03.

tools.name: google/gemma-4-31B-it
tools.what: The Gemma 4 successor at about 31 billion parameters, images and text, two safetensors shards, Apache-2.0 as the hub reports it, and ungated.

tools.name: huggingface/text-generation-inference
tools.what: A server process that holds weights and answers completion calls, the same role as vLLM.

tools.name: LM Studio
tools.what: A closed desktop application that downloads and serves models on a workstation.

tools.name: meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
tools.what: Meta’s 8-billion-parameter instruction-tuned text model, tagged for eight languages, published as four safetensors shards plus one PyTorch checkpoint under Meta’s own Llama 3.1 licence and behind a manual approval gate; the card body returned 401 without a login on 2026-09-03.

tools.name: mistralai/Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.3
tools.what: Mistral’s 7-billion-parameter instruction-tuned text model, Apache-2.0 as the hub reports it, ungated, four safetensors shards, and tagged for vLLM rather than for the transformers library; its card says it is the instruct fine-tune of Mistral-7B-v0.3.

tools.name: ollama/ollama
tools.what: A local server plus CLI that pulls a packaged model and serves it on a workstation.

tools.name: openai/gpt-oss-120b
tools.what: The larger of OpenAI’s two open-weight text models, about 117 billion parameters in the same 4-bit mxfp4 packing as its sibling, 22 safetensors shards, Apache-2.0, ungated.

tools.name: openai/gpt-oss-20b
tools.what: OpenAI’s smaller open-weight text model, about 21 billion parameters, most of them stored in the 4-bit packing the hub tags as mxfp4 so the shards weigh far less than the count suggests; Apache-2.0, ungated, tagged for vLLM and transformers.

tools.name: Qwen/Qwen3-8B
tools.what: An 8-billion-parameter dense text model from Alibaba’s Qwen team, Apache-2.0, ungated, five safetensors shards, configuration model type qwen3; its card describes Qwen3 as a family of dense and mixture-of-experts models, of which this is a small dense member.

tools.name: Qwen/Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B
tools.what: A mixture-of-experts text model of about 2.4 trillion parameters in 213 safetensors shards, under a vendor-named license (qwen3.8-max) the hub reports as ‘other’, ungated.

tools.name: Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next
tools.what: A Qwen model that takes images as well as text (the hub files it as image-text-to-text), about 180 billion parameters in 131 safetensors shards, under a vendor-named licence (Qwen Community 1.0) the hub reports as ‘other’.

tools.name: vllm-project/vllm
tools.what: A Python library and a server process that holds model weights in GPU memory and answers completion calls over an OpenAI-shaped API.

tools.name: AWS Bedrock
tools.what: A managed API in front of many vendors’ models. You do not run a serving process and you cannot read one: what you obtain is an endpoint and a bill, and the gateway and serving layers are collapsed behind it.

tools.name: BerriAI/litellm
tools.what: Two shapes in one repository: a Python SDK you import, and a proxy server you deploy in front of many providers.

tools.name: Martian
tools.what: Classified here as a model router. Its homepage leads with interpretability research rather than routing. Nobody here has read the documentation, so that is a homepage and not the product.

tools.name: Not Diamond
tools.what: A router that chooses which model answers, sold on cost against frontier quality.

tools.name: OpenRouter
tools.what: A hosted gateway in front of many vendors’ models. You obtain an endpoint and a bill; there is no serving process to read and no gateway process you run, so both layers are collapsed behind somebody else’s API.

tools.name: Portkey
tools.what: A hosted gateway whose distinguishing claim is what it records about each call rather than what it routes.

tools.name: andrewyng/context-hub
tools.what: A curated set of reference documentation for third-party SDKs and APIs, reached through a CLI (chub) or an MCP server (chub-mcp), with entries annotated and corrected by pull request.

tools.name: Glean
tools.what: A hosted index over an organization’s own SaaS sources, reached as a service.

tools.name: upstash/context7
tools.what: An MCP server that supplies up-to-date library documentation to a coding agent.

tools.name: Claude Agent SDK
tools.what: A harness you import rather than a process you deploy, which is why it sits on orchestration and not on interface: the party sitting in front of it is your own program.

tools.name: Claude Managed Agents
tools.what: A hosted service from Anthropic, in beta, that runs an agent for you: it holds the loop that decides the next step, and it supplies the sandbox the agent’s tools run in, either in Anthropic’s cloud or on your own infrastructure through a worker process you run.

tools.name: crewAIInc/crewAI
tools.what: A Python library you import. Role-based agents with a declared crew, plus an event-driven Flows API.

tools.name: langchain-ai/langgraph
tools.what: A library you import into your own process, in Python or TypeScript.

tools.name: mastra-ai/mastra
tools.what: A TypeScript framework you import, shipped as one bundle rather than assembled parts, deployable as a standalone server.

tools.name: microsoft/agent-framework
tools.what: A library you import, in .NET and Python. The README at the read sha also names Go.

tools.name: temporalio/temporal
tools.what: A server you run, plus per-language client SDKs you import. The workflow code lives in your process; the server holds the durable state and replays it.

tools.name: Amazon Q Developer
tools.what: An AWS-side coding assistant with an editor plugin, a CLI and a hosted surface.

tools.name: anomalyco/opencode
tools.what: A terminal coding agent, installed as a binary or an npm package. It holds the loop, chooses tools and manages context, and its source is readable.

tools.name: ChatGPT
tools.what: A hosted assistant reached in a browser, a desktop application and mobile clients.

tools.name: Claude Code
tools.what: A coding agent from Anthropic that you run in a terminal or an editor, among four surfaces: you state work in words and it holds the conversation, chooses which tools to call, runs commands and manages its own context until the work is done or it stops to ask.

tools.name: Cursor
tools.what: An editor with an agent built into it, which is why it sits on the line between something a person sits in front of and the thing holding the loop.

tools.name: FlowiseAI/Flowise
tools.what: A Node server you run with a visual builder over it. The README at the read sha opens by saying the project has been archived and points at a discussion, and the API reports archived: true, so what a reader obtains is a frozen tree.

tools.name: Gemini Code Assist
tools.what: Google’s editor-side coding assistant, sold to organizations rather than to the browser user the Gemini row covers.

tools.name: GitHub Copilot
tools.what: Several products under one name: an inline completion extension in an editor, a chat surface, a CLI, and a coding agent that opens pull requests.

tools.name: Google Gemini
tools.what: Google’s hosted chat assistant, the consumer product rather than the developer tooling. Three separately named things ship under that one word, and the other two have their own rows below.

tools.name: google-gemini/gemini-cli
tools.what: A terminal agent installed from npm or a package manager, holding the loop and calling tools, extensible over MCP.

tools.name: Kiro
tools.what: An editor that owns the editing surface, like Cursor, and frames its workflow around specs rather than around chat.

tools.name: langflow-ai/langflow
tools.what: A server you run with a visual authoring surface, which also exposes every workflow as an API and an MCP server.

tools.name: langgenius/dify
tools.what: A server you run, or a hosted tier, presenting a builder over a workflow engine, a RAG pipeline and model management.

tools.name: lmstudio-ai/lms
tools.what: A CLI that ships with the LM Studio desktop application and drives it.

tools.name: Microsoft Copilot Studio
tools.what: A hosted builder for agents, licensed inside Microsoft 365 rather than bought separately.

tools.name: n8n-io/n8n
tools.what: A server you run (or a hosted tier) with a visual canvas over it.

tools.name: openai/codex
tools.what: A coding agent installed as a local binary, with an IDE extension and a cloud surface named separately by the same README.

tools.name: Relevance AI
tools.what: A hosted builder aimed at business functions rather than at engineering. You do not own the runtime it executes on.

tools.name: Stack AI
tools.what: A hosted drag-and-drop builder aimed at enterprise deployment. Its own page leads with security and compliance rather than with capability, which is the axis a closed builder competes on once several of them can draw the same graph.

tools.name: Vellum
tools.what: Filed as an agent-evaluation service, but its own page, read 2026-09-03, describes a personal AI assistant with persistent memory and says nothing about evaluation. Which of those is the product could not be established.

tools.name: addyosmani/agent-skills
tools.what: 25 skill directories under skills/, named for lifecycle phases, planning, TDD, code review, debugging, security, shipping.

tools.name: agentskills/agentskills
tools.what: The specification plus a validator. The published spec at agentskills.io/specification, read on 2026-09-10, defines six frontmatter fields: name and description required, license, compatibility, metadata and allowed-tools optional.

tools.name: anthropics/skills
tools.what: A repository of skill directories. Each holds a skill.md plus its scripts and resources, and nothing in the repository runs: a harness that implements the Agent Skills standard loads a directory.

tools.name: ComposioHQ/awesome-claude-skills
tools.what: Both a list and an implementation, which is why one word for it is wrong.

tools.name: github/spec-kit
tools.what: A CLI that writes a scaffold of prompts and templates into a repository, agent-agnostic across many coding agents.

tools.name: jax-ml/jax
tools.what: A Python library for array computation and program transformation, with automatic differentiation and compilation to accelerators.

tools.name: mattpocock/skills
tools.what: 37 skill directories under skills/, grouped engineering/, productivity/, misc/ and in-progress/, published as a Claude Code plugin with a .claude-plugin/marketplace.json.

tools.name: ml-explore/mlx
tools.what: An array framework you import, targeting Apple silicon’s unified memory, for build-time and on-device use at once.

tools.name: ml-explore/mlx-lm
tools.what: A Python package over mlx for generating text and fine-tuning language models on Apple silicon.

tools.name: obra/superpowers
tools.what: A methodology shipped as files. 14 skill directories under skills/, plus hooks, scripts and tests, and a separate plugin manifest for each of eight harnesses in the same tree: .claude-plugin/, .codex-plugin/, .cursor-plugin/, .devin-plugin/, .hermes-plugin/, .kimi-plugin/, .opencode/ and .pi/, alongside root agents.md, claude.md, gemini.md and gemini-extension.json.

tools.name: pytorch/pytorch
tools.what: A Python package you import, with compiled kernels underneath. Build-time: it trains and defines models, and is not on the request path a served model answers from.

tools.name: tensorflow/tensorflow
tools.what: A framework you import, with a large surrounding ecosystem of tools and libraries.

tools.name: agentic-community/mcp-gateway-registry
tools.what: An MCP gateway and registry: one governed address that agents discover MCP servers from once those servers are scattered.

tools.name: LangSmith Context Hub
tools.what: A hosted registry for the prompts and contexts an agent loads, versioned and environment-tagged.

tools.name: Microsoft Agent 365
tools.what: A hosted place to register and manage agents. Its vendor-neutrality is a claim reproduced here and not checked: nobody here has tested it against the product.

tools.name: mlflow/mlflow
tools.what: A server plus client libraries. Runs, parameters, artifacts and registered model versions go in; the registry half is what makes it a versioning surface rather than only a logging one.

tools.name: Infisical/infisical
tools.what: A self-hosted service (with a managed tier) that holds secrets and brokers credentials on an outbound call, so the agent holds a placeholder and never the real value.
